channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: Venezuela después del pacto petrolero con EE. UU.
item.description: La administración Trump ha anunciado un acuerdo con Caracas que, según dice, otorga a EE. UU. una participación importante en la industria petrolera venezolana. En esta sesión de preguntas y respuestas, los expertos de Crisis Group Phil Gunson y Delaney Simon analizan las repercusiones de dicho acuerdo. Venezuela después del pacto petrolero con EE.

item.title: Michelle Bachelet withdraws from race to become UN secretary general
item.description: Former president of Chile drops out after support collapsed in security council straw poll, leaving seven candidates in contestMichelle Bachelet, a former president of Chile, has withdrawn her candidacy to become the next secretary general of the ⁠UN, ending an attempt ​that had struggled to gain traction among security council members. Michelle Bachelet withdraws from race to become UN secretary general.

item.title: Brazil, India are building strategic ties for a changing world, says Brazil’s Foreign Minister
item.description: On whether BRICS seeks to replace the U. S. dollar, the Brazilian envoy says the possible use of local currencies for settling part of bilateral trade is something many countries already do, and that governments do not tell companies which currency they must use Brazil, India are building strategic ties for a changing world, says Brazil’s Foreign Minister.

item.title: Afghan Minaret Restoration Marks 'Pragmatic' Taliban Approach To Cultural Heritage, Experts Say
item.description: Work is now underway to the restore Afghanistan's Minaret of Jam, which experts say reflects a welcome departure from the icon-smashing rule of the Taliban of the 1990s. The change contrasts with the current Taliban rulers' draconian restrictions on other facets of life in the country. Afghan Minaret Restoration Marks 'Pragmatic' Taliban Approach To Cultural Heritage, Experts Say.

item.title: Indonesia rescue agency recovers another victim from capsized ship, authorities say
item.description: The passenger ship Virgo Transport 8 was carrying 243 people, including 30 crew members, when it capsized in bad weather early on Sep 13 during a voyage from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan. Indonesia rescue agency recovers another victim from capsized ship, authorities say.

item.title: Russia's Starlink Rival Faces Problems In Orbit And Threats On The Ground
item.description: Russia is racing to build Rassvet, its answer to Starlink, after losing access to the satellite network on the battlefield in Ukraine. But troubled satellites, tight deadlines, and a lack of ground terminals could leave Moscow waiting years. Russia's Starlink Rival Faces Problems In Orbit And Threats On The Ground.

item.title: Russian election, cast as test of support for Ukraine war, enters final day
item.description: Most anti-war candidates ‌were barred from the ballot; those who did run from the liberal Yabloko party said they feared for their freedom after courts handed long jail terms to two senior party figures before the vote for comments about the conflict deemed illegal by authorities Russian election, cast as test of support for Ukraine war, enters final day.

item.title: North Korea fires unidentified projectile into East Sea: Seoul
item.description: The launch came eight days after North Korea fired multiple short-range ballistic missiles towards the East Sea - also called the Sea of Japan - as part of what it later described as a joint firepower drill. North Korea fires unidentified projectile into East Sea: Seoul.

item.title: Najib says unable to pay US$12.26m fine for house arrest pardon; assets 'not within his sole
item.description: Najib Razak said he cannot pay the US$12.26 million fine tied to his house‑arrest pardon. A statement released by the former Malaysian prime minister's legal team on Sunday (Sep 20) said a significant part of Najib Razak’s assets, bank accounts and properties remained subject to freezing orders and enforcement proceedings by the government. Najib says unable to pay US$12.26m fine for house arrest pardon; assets 'not within his sole.

item.title: Why China is pushing back on US warnings over rapid AI development
item.description: Beijing believes slowdown calls aim to lock in US advantage, and is pursuing a different balance between safety and paceAbout two years ago, education entrepreneur Boris But had what he calls a “penny-drop moment” – that, like countless others in China, his company needed to embrace AI before it was made obsolete by it. Why China is pushing back on US warnings over rapid AI development.

item.title: China pairs undersea drone mothership with multidomain war vision
item.description: China is constructing what may be the world’s first dedicated mothership for extra-extra-large uncrewed underwater vehicles (XXLUUVs) at the Hudong-Zhonghua shipyard in Shanghai, multiple outlets reported. Satellite photos show the roughly 200-meter hull features a large internal hangar. likely capable of stowing up to four autonomous submersibles. and an open-bottom stern well-deck fitted [] T China pairs undersea drone mothership with multidomain war vision.

item.title: Trump Signs Russia-Iran Sanctions Bill, Putting New Pressure Tools At His Disposal
item.description: US President Donald Trump signed into law legislation aimed at increasing economic pressure on Russia over its war on Ukraine, including by targeting Moscow's energy revenues as well as countries that continue to buy Russian oil and gas. Trump Signs Russia-Iran Sanctions Bill, Putting New Pressure Tools At His Disposal.

item.title: US-Saudi F-35 fighter deal runs into a China-sized problem
item.description: A potential multi-billion-dollar transfer of advanced US stealth fighters to Saudi Arabia has thrust US Middle East policy into a delicate balancing act between regional deterrence, Israeli air superiority and rising geopolitical skepticism. The US State Department approved a potential US$24.3 billion Foreign Military Sale (FMS) of 48 Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II fighter jets [] The post US- US-Saudi F-35 fighter deal runs into a China-sized problem.

item.title: Suicide Attack On Police Facility In Northwest Pakistan Leaves Many Dead And Wounded
item.description: At least 16 people were reported dead and dozens were injured after an attacker drove a vehicle packed with explosives into a police complex in Pakistan. Officials said several other attackers died in a shootout with police after the blast in the city of Kohat in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province. Suicide Attack On Police Facility In Northwest Pakistan Leaves Many Dead And Wounded.

item.title: Brazil’s Lula announces higher welfare payments and free weight-loss jabs ahead of election
item.description: Critics say moves from leftwing incumbent president are electorally motivated two weeks before Brazil’s electionsBrazil’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has announced a 15% increase in the country’s main cash-transfer programme for poor families, as well as free weight-loss jabs, prompting criticism from opponents who say the moves are electorally motivated just two weeks before the preside Brazil’s Lula announces higher welfare payments and free weight-loss jabs ahead of election.

item.title: Technology is transforming crime – and the response to it
item.description: Sitting in her Vienna office ahead of a pivotal UN gathering in Abu Dhabi, Monica Juma is focused on a simple reality: crime has evolved faster than many of the institutions designed to combat it. Technology is transforming crime – and the response to it.

item.title: ‘Violence will only defer a problem’: UN Assembly President on trust, AI and lessons from the
item.description: Khalilur Rahman took the gavel as President of the UN General Assembly's 81st session amid what he calls a crisis of confidence in the organization he has served – in one capacity or another – for 35 years. ‘Violence will only defer a problem’: UN Assembly President on trust, AI and lessons from the.

item.title: Security Council LIVE: UN peacekeeping under pressure
item.description: UN peacekeepers have increasingly been sent into places where there is no peace to keep – under resourced, outgunned and exposed to violence they are not equipped to counter. The Security Council meets this afternoon in New York to confront that problem, with Secretary-General António Guterres briefing ambassadors on how to close the gap. Security Council LIVE: UN peacekeeping under pressure.

item.title: Women and girls pay high price in DR Congo Ebola outbreak
item.description: The deadly Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has taken a disproportionate toll on women and girls, many of whom are on the frontlines caring for patients as well as their own families despite the high risk of infection. Women and girls pay high price in DR Congo Ebola outbreak.

item.title: Child malnutrition crisis worsens amid escalating violence
item.description: Haiti is facing a worsening child malnutrition crisis, with an estimated 253,725 children aged 6 to 59 months projected to suffer from acute malnutrition between June 2026 and May 2027, new UN-backed analysis has revealed. Child malnutrition crisis worsens amid escalating violence.
